name: Bisoprolol
owner: generic (many); Concor brand held by Merck KGaA

discovery.note: Developed in Germany in the 1970s–80s; first marketed in Europe as Concor.

tagline: Highly β1-selective once-daily beta-blocker proven in heart failure
summary: Bisoprolol is one of the most β1-selective beta-blockers, with balanced renal and hepatic clearance and once-daily dosing. It treats hypertension and angina and, after the CIBIS-II trial, is a standard therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
mechanism: Bisoprolol competitively blocks β1-adrenoceptors with high selectivity, slowing the heart, reducing contractility and lowering renin release.
In heart failure, long-term sympathetic blockade reduces arrhythmias, myocyte toxicity and adverse remodelling, improving survival when titrated slowly.
uses: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Zebeta for hypertension.

history.title: Ziac
history.detail: A low-dose combination with hydrochlorothiazide is approved in the US as first-line therapy.

history.title: CIBIS
history.detail: The first Cardiac Insufficiency Bisoprolol Study shows a trend toward lower mortality in heart failure without reaching significance, prompting the larger CIBIS-II.

history.title: CIBIS-II
history.detail: Bisoprolol reduces all-cause mortality by 34% in chronic heart failure; the trial is stopped early.

history.title: CIBIS-III
history.detail: Starting heart-failure treatment with bisoprolol is non-inferior to starting with enalapril, supporting either order of initiation.

facts: It is the beta-blocker listed on the WHO Model List, with metoprolol and carvedilol as alternatives.

references.title: CIBIS-II Investigators. The Cardiac Insufficiency Bisoprolol Study II. Lancet 1999
